title: Architecting and Testing Controllable Agents: Lance Martin
talk_summary: Lance Martin argues that reliable agents come from constraining LLM control flow with explicit graphs/state machines, using LLMs only at discrete decision points, and testing both final answers and tool-call trajectories. He also shows cheap in-app checks, explicit routing, recursion limits, and retrieval/context decoupling as practical reliability mechanisms.

takeaways.technique: Constrain recurring agent workflows as explicit graphs
takeaways.what_they_do: Use developer-defined nodes/edges for fixed stages and insert LLM decisions only at specific gates, instead of letting a ReAct loop choose arbitrary tool sequences.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Lang graph kind of sits in the Middle where you can actually Implement these userdefined SL llm gated control flows
takeaways.numbers: LangGraph tool-call trajectory stayed consistent across 8B and 70B models; React trajectories degraded even with GPT-4o.

takeaways.technique: Evaluate tool-call trajectories, not just final output
takeaways.what_they_do: Log step names per graph node or extract tool calls from message history, then compare runs against canonical expected trajectories; for open-ended runs, check for repeated calls, excessive calls, or missing required tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I compare the tool calls that the thing did to these trajectories
takeaways.numbers: 5-question eval; LangGraph reached 100% tool trajectory and 60-80% answer correctness; React tool trajectories were degraded.

takeaways.technique: Inline lightweight unit tests and schema checks for self-correction
takeaways.what_they_do: Run cheap deterministic checks inside the agent loop, such as import checks, code execution, or schema validation, and feed failures back to the LLM to retry before finishing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: simple unit test like this can actually run in your app itself
takeaways.numbers: Import-check unit test significantly improved internal RAG code-generation performance; unit tests are fast and cheap.

takeaways.technique: Explicit router node before model/tool selection
takeaways.what_they_do: Put a dedicated routing step at the start of the workflow to classify the request and send it to one of a few paths; for many tools, use semantic similarity over verbose tool descriptions to shortlist tools.

takeaways.technique: Decouple retrieval chunks from generation context
takeaways.what_they_do: Index small chunks for retrieval, but store/reference full documents or sections and pass the larger context to the LLM for generation; use metadata/reranking to promote canonical docs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: decoupling what you actually index for retrieval from what you pass the llm

takeaways.what_they_do: Set a max recursion/step limit in graph config and persist a compact state dictionary across the run so long tasks can stop, resume, or avoid infinite loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: set a recursion limit in your Lang graph config so you basically tell it to only proceed for some number of cycles
takeaways.numbers: Default recursion limit cited around 20 cycles.
